card.intuition: Training is the one-time, expensive process by which a model provider sets a model's parameters, exposing the model to trillions of tokens and nudging weights toward better next-token prediction. Everything the model 'knows' is a side effect of getting better at prediction, compressed into the parameters. Training ends at a point in time, which is why the model ships with a knowledge cutoff.
card.analogy: A months-long apprenticeship the employer pays for: the operator ships with everything baked into habit as of day one, and days of field corrections change none of it — refreshing the habits means another apprenticeship.
card.time_complexity: Training is the highest-cost phase — one massive provider-side compute run over trillions of tokens — which is why you pay per inference request instead; retraining is effectively out of reach per project.
card.space_complexity: Training consumes the provider's hardware and the raw corpus, not your context window, so its footprint on your side is zero — the product 'lives' only in the parameters it delivers.
when_to_use: Explaining why the model's built-in knowledge stops at its knowledge cutoff
Choosing context injection over training when a model doesn't know your internal APIs
Understanding why per-request inference pricing exists at all
Distinguishing pre-training from post-training refinements like instruction-following and safety
gotchas: Training is not something you can do: when the model doesn't know your codebase, the fix is context, not teaching
The model's facts are side effects of prediction, not a stored database it consults

steps.label: Corpus
steps.annotation: Vast amounts of text are exposed to the model.

steps.label: Predict
steps.annotation: The model predicts the next token for each stretch of text.

steps.label: Adjust
steps.annotation: Parameters are nudged toward whatever the actual next token was.

steps.label: Repeat
steps.annotation: The loop repeats across the corpus until the parameters converge.

steps.label: Ship
steps.annotation: Training ends, parameters freeze, and the model carries a knowledge cutoff.

steps.label: Post-train
steps.annotation: Later post-training shapes instruction-following and safety behavior.
